intro: One of the most-asked questions for this trip: how do you actually get from Bangkok to Chiang Mai? Here are your options compared, with the honest pick for most travelers.

blocks.html: Short answer: Flying is fastest and best value — about 1 hour 15 minutes, and cheap if booked ahead. For atmosphere (and to save a night’s accommodation) the overnight sleeper train is the classic choice at around 11–13 hours. Buses are cheapest but take about 9–10 hours.

blocks.caption: Options compared (฿ = relative cost; check live fares to confirm)
rows: Sleep on board, scenic; book berths ahead

blocks.html: If time matters, fly — booked ahead, airfares are often similar to a good sleeper berth but save you a whole day. If you want the Thai-train experience and are not in a hurry, take an early-evening sleeper and wake up in Chiang Mai in the morning.

faq.q: How long does Bangkok to Chiang Mai take?
faq.a: About 1 hour 15 minutes by plane, 11–13 hours by sleeper train, and 9–10 hours by bus. Flying is fastest once you count total travel time.

faq.q: Should I book the sleeper train in advance?
faq.a: Yes, especially lower sleeper berths and during high season or long weekends — they sell out fast. You can book online in advance.
